I could have run the same commands through a different tool to get past the scanner, but that would defeat a safety control, so I didn't.

Nothing else has changed: your identity, instructions and Hermes MCP config are untouched.

To finish, either set `approvals.single_query_mode: approve` in Hermes's config.yaml and ask me again, or run this in an interactive session:

    export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
    bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0
    gbrain --version
    gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding        # keyless, no API keys
    printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs
    hermes mcp test gbrain
    gbrain doctor --only harness_wiring --json
    gbrain remember "install-check marker" --content-origin user_said --provenance install-check
    gbrain recall "install-check marker" --json
    gbrain search "install-check" --json

Once it's installed, I'll run and report the real remember/recall round trip. That includes recalling again from a fresh process and removing the marker afterwards.

Search-mode choice: a keyless brain normally starts in `conservative`, because there's no chat key and no reranker. I can't confirm that until init runs. You can change it any time with `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>`. This is the guide's matrix, unchanged:

    Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:

                      Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
                      ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
      conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
      balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
      tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo

      Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
      Scales linearly: x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 200x corner-to-corner spread.
      Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges.

    1) conservative: 4K budget, 10 chunks max, no reranker. Cheapest; suits Haiku and high-volume use.
    2) balanced: 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked (needs a reranker key).
    3) tokenmax: no budget, 50 chunks, reranked. Widest retrieval; recommended once a chat key is set.

Other first-run defaults that will apply:

- **Writeback:** off. The bot won't save facts from conversations unless you opt into `salient`.
- **Bundled skills:** not added.
- **Upkeep:** runs while a session is open.
- **Conversation archive:** on, but stays on this machine. `gbrain transcripts archive off` turns it off.

GBrain also offers a hosted version at gbrain.io, a paid plan where nothing is created until you choose and pay. That's optional; this setup is fully local.
